results.title: The Sahel’s terrorism epicenter is the Mali-Burkina Faso-Niger tri-border (Liptako-Gourma).
results.description: The Sahel’s terrorism epicenter is the Mali-Burkina Faso-Niger tri-border (Liptako-Gourma). Per AFRICOM and Global Terrorism Index data, it drives over half of worldwide terror deaths. JNIM (al-Qaeda affiliate, 7-8k fighters) dominates with expansions, blockades, and attacks into coastal states and mining areas. Rival ISSP (IS, ~2k fighters) contests it fiercely—recent Oct 2026 clashes claimed 400+ dead. After Western exits, AES juntas rely on Russian Africa Corps; groups exploit weak governance and local grievances, sustaining high violence and spillover risks.

results.title: Africa Corps under pressure: the 🌴Sahel, April–October 2026 Russia promised security to the Sahel’s military regimes.
results.description:
Africa Corps under pressure: the 🌴Sahel, April–October 2026

Russia promised security to the Sahel’s military regimes. The facts tell a different story.

🇲🇱 Mali: On 25 April, coordinated 🥷JNIM and FLA attacks struck several locations, including Bamako and Kati. Defence Minister Sadio Camara was killed and Kidal fell to the FLA. On 10 September, JNIM overran Dioura, reportedly killing over 100 Malian soldiers and five Africa Corps personnel. Russian-backed forces returned to Kidal in October after the FLA withdrew—but holding it remains the real test.

🇧🇫 Burkina Faso: JNIM continues to inflict heavy losses. At least 34 civilians were reportedly executed in Titao in February; around 90 soldiers were reportedly killed in a September ambush at Koubel-Alpha.

🇳🇪 Niger: More than 50 security personnel were reportedly killed in two September attacks. Even Niamey’s military infrastructure has been targeted. Africa Corps has not stopped the insurgency.

The verdict: Russia’s presence has not delivered security. The 🇺🇸US State Department advises Americans NOT TO TRAVEL to all three AES countries.

#AES #Sahel #Mali #BurkinaFaso #Niger #JNIM

results.title: Obasanjo is only repeating the obvious here.
results.description:
Obasanjo is only repeating the obvious here.

All sensible people knew that Bola @officialABAT’s gross incompetence triggered the Sahel Nations out of ECOWAS.
He wanted to prove his renewed subservience to President Macron of France 🇫🇷 , so he naively sanctioned Niger Republic 🇳🇪 and threatened to invade the country unless the toppled President Bazoum was reinstated within an ultimatum.

But Niger is a country that doesn’t take external threats lightly. In 2009 when President Tandja Mamadou organised and won a referendum for tenure extension, Niger was suspended from the ECOWAS. The Nigerien officials responded strongly, reminding ECOWAS that countries make up the block, not the other way round, and threatened to leave if the interference in their internal affairs continued.

The only thing that stopped adamant Niger’s breakaway then was possibly the military coup led by Salou Djibo in early 2010. Nigeria was happy with the coup then, as it was even alleged that General Abdulsalam Abubakar, who led ECOWAS delegation to the country in 2009, effectively planned the coup during his mission in Niger.

Fast forwarded to 2023, similar scenario played out in Niger 🇳🇪, where Soldiers led by Abdourahamane Tciani overthrew President Mohamed Bazoum after serving just 2 years of his 5-year mandate.

But this time around, Nigeria is unhappy with the coup. So, Bola and his inept advisers who lack knowledge of history and international affairs or willingly ignored both to carry out the command of their “slavemaster” France, whose interests are threatened by Bazoum’s removal, responded with an unprecedentedly disdainful and hostile threat against the Nigerien Junta.

If civilian officials of Niger strongly rejected much lesser threats in 2009, what would anyone expect of their Military, 14 years later?

Niger is a good neighbour and a key stakeholder in the Multinational Joint Task Force (MNJTF) that helps in the fight against terrorism affecting our country and the broader Sahel region. They help us with intelligence and even live data about terrorists movements. Above all, they helped us in the Civil War and played a significant role in keeping Nigeria as one country which Bola now enjoys to govern.

But all that did not matter to Bola and his disastrous regime.

All he and his failed NSA Nuhu @NuhuRibadu (aka DPO) care about is politics rather than protecting the lives and properties of citizens, then claiming credit for a “rescue” by ONSA (or is it ONGA)’s “tactical team” after citizens have paid ransom to get their loved ones released.

Oya, let the blockheaded BATidiots start abusing Obasanjo. They’ve been hailing him on remarks against Atiku.

results.title: When Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger left ECOWAS last year, many of us felt the ripple in markets and border posts.
results.description:
When Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger left ECOWAS last year, many of us felt the ripple in markets and border posts. Last week in Dakar the two sides sat down properly and agreed to build a practical cooperation framework — not a return to membership, but rules that could ease trade, movement and security cooperation.
Ordinary people have been paying the price of the split in higher costs and delays. If these working groups deliver clear, fair rules, that is what actually matters on the ground. The question is whether we keep the focus on livelihoods or let process swallow the purpose.
This is Society & Diplomacy. Where Global Issues Meet Everyday Life.
#SocietyAndDiplomacy 
#HalimaAbdullah

results.title: 🔘 US Security Analysis Warns of ISIS-Sahel Networks Extending Toward Morocco and Spain Rabat | October 23, 2026 A security analysis publishe
results.description:
🔘 US Security Analysis Warns of ISIS-Sahel Networks Extending Toward Morocco and Spain

Rabat | October 23, 2026

A security analysis published by the US-based platform Lawfare on October 18 highlights the evolving transnational threat posed by Islamic State networks operating across Africa's Sahel region, including potential links to Morocco and Spain.

The assessment examines recruitment, financing and remote operational coordination, drawing on counterterrorism investigations and previously disrupted networks.

The warning comes amid persistent jihadist violence in the Sahel. Reuters reported that at least 48 civilians were killed in attacks in eastern Mali attributed by local sources to Islamic State-linked militants.

For Morocco, these developments underscore the strategic importance of preventive intelligence, cross-border security cooperation and early disruption of extremist networks.

The available reporting does not establish an imminent terrorist attack in Morocco.

#Morocco #SahelSecurity #Counterterrorism #StrategicInsight #NajibStrategy #NajibCommunication
